overview: This one-page file consists of a State Department transmittal dated May 9, 1930, forwarding to the U.S. Treasury Department a copy of Tokyo Embassy despatch No. 86 of April 7, 1930, concerning the control of opium addiction in Formosa (Taiwan). The referenced despatch is listed as an enclosure but is not present in the supplied pages.

subfiles.summary: Referring to an earlier departmental letter of April 2, 1930, the Secretary of State transmits for the Treasury Secretary’s information a copy of despatch No. 86 from the Embassy at Tokyo. The despatch, dated April 7, 1930, concerns measures for controlling opium addiction in Formosa. Although identified as an enclosure, the copy of the despatch is not included in the supplied file text.

interest: The document illustrates routine interdepartmental circulation of overseas diplomatic reporting on narcotics policy, linking the State Department, the Treasury Department’s Division of Foreign Control, and the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo. It also points to American official interest in opium-addiction controls in colonial Taiwan under Japanese rule. The absence of the cited enclosure is itself archivally useful, since the page preserves its despatch number and date for tracing elsewhere in the record series.
